steps: The Drilling operation uses a Drill Press to create a 12 mm hole in a Metal bar placed on a ConveyorBelt with a spindle speed of 1200 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, transforming it into a Drilled component placed on a MobileRobot, and takes 91 minutes to complete.

Using a Broaching Machine for 20 minutes, a metal bar from the conveyor belt is transformed into a broached component with a keyway broach, operating at a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev and a depth of cut of 5 mm, and the resulting component is placed on a mobile robot.

The Sheet Metal Shear machine shears the sheet metal from the conveyor belt into sheared sheet metal at a 90° angle and a cutting speed of 10 m/min using a straight blade, taking 60 minutes to complete the operation, with the output placed on a mobile robot.

The Vertical Milling Machine performs vertical milling on a lathed part from the conveyor belt for 13 minutes using an end mill at 800 rpm with a depth of cut of 2 mm, producing a milled part that is placed on the mobile robot.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) for 54 minutes, the shaped part from the conveyor belt is precision machined into a finished part, which is then placed on a mobile robot, with key parameters including a voltage of 50 V, a current of 10 A, a brass wire, and a cutting speed of 6 mm/min.

A Vertical Lathe performs Vertical Turning on a Metal bar for 69 minutes at a rotation speed of 1500 rpm, using a Carbide insert tool with a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, transforming the Metal bar into a Lathed part that is then placed on a Mobile Robot.

The CNC Turning operation shapes a lathed part from the conveyor belt into a finished machined component using a CNC Turning Center for 78 minutes, with a spindle speed of 2000 rpm, tool offsets of X=0.1 and Z=0.05, and a G-code program.

The drilling operation uses an 8 mm drill at a spindle speed of 1500 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev on the Drill Press for 32 minutes, transforming a Metal bar from the ConveyorBelt into a Drilled component placed on the MobileRobot.

Perform High-Precision Milling on a Stewart Platform Mills for 47 minutes, using a ball end mill with a milling precision of 0.01 mm and active vibration damping, to transform a milled part from the conveyor belt into a ground part loaded onto a mobile robot.

Using a Horizontal Lathe, perform Horizontal Turning on a Metal bar from the ConveyorBelt for 81 minutes at a rotation speed of 1200 rpm, a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, and with a Ceramic insert tool to produce a Lathed part, which is then placed on a MobileRobot.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs the Horizontal Milling operation on a Milled part taken from the ConveyorBelt for 96 minutes at a milling speed of 1000 rpm with a linear tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.4, producing a Finished machined component placed on the MobileRobot.

The Gear Shaping operation uses a Gear Shaper to transform a Broached component into a Shaped gear with 24 teeth of Spur type, running at a shaping speed of 50 rpm, for 69 minutes, with the input component sourced from a ConveyorBelt and the output product transferred to a MobileRobot.

The Gear Shaping operation shapes a broached component into a helical gear with 30 teeth using a Gear Shaper at a shaping speed of 40 rpm for 74 minutes, resulting in a shaped gear ready for transport on a mobile robot.

The Shaper machine performs a shaping operation on a milled part taken from the conveyor belt, using a single-point tool with a stroke length of 200 mm and a shaping speed of 30 strokes/min, transforming it into a shaped part placed on the mobile robot, for 67 minutes.

Using a Shaper machine, perform Shaping for 74 minutes on a Milled Shaft retrieved from the ConveyorBelt, with a stroke length of 100mm, shaping speed of 0.2 mm/rev, and an HSS Cutter tool, to produce a Shaped Shaft transferred to a MobileRobot.

Using a Horizontal Lathe, a steel bar from the conveyor belt is turned into a lathed shaft for 12 minutes at a rotation speed of 800 rpm, a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, and with a carbide tool, resulting in the finished part being placed on a mobile robot.

Using a Grinding Machine for 52 minutes, the Planed Shaft is ground into a Ground Shaft using an Aluminum Oxide grinding wheel at 1800 rpm with a feed rate of 0.05 mm/rev, transferring the input from the ConveyorBelt and outputting to the MobileRobot.

The CNC Turning operation on the CNC Turning Center machines a Lathed Shaft from the ConveyorBelt into a Finished Shaft for 13 minutes using a G-code program with a spindle speed of 1000 rpm and tool offsets of 0.01mm, then places the finished component on a MobileRobot.

The Stewart Platform Mills perform milling for 4 minutes with a precision of 0.001mm using an End Mill tool configuration and active vibration damping, transforming a Milled Shaft from the ConveyorBelt into a Ground Shaft placed on a MobileRobot.

Using Screw Machines for 36 minutes, the Screw Cutting operation processes a Lathed Shaft from the ConveyorBelt into a Threaded Shaft, which is placed on a MobileRobot, with parameters including an M12 screw size, Metric thread type, and a production rate of 10 pcs/min.

The Gear Shaper performs Gear Shaping on a Broached Shaft for 69 minutes to produce a Shaped Gear, using a Helical gear type with 25 teeth and a shaping speed of 0.15 mm/rev, with input from the ConveyorBelt and output to the MobileRobot.

The Hobbing Machine performs hobbing on a Broached Shaft from the Conveyor Belt at a speed of 0.2 mm/rev and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/rev to create an Involute gear profile, producing a Hobbied Gear that is placed on the Mobile Robot, with the operation taking 5 minutes.
Using a Vertical Lathe, the Turning operation transforms a Steel Bar into a Lathed Shaft over 21 minutes with a rotation speed of 700 rpm, a ceramic tool, and a feed rate of 0.12 mm/rev.

The Vertical Milling Machine performs the Milling operation for 57 minutes, using a Carbide End Mill at a speed of 1200 rpm and a depth of cut of 0.3 mm, to transform the Lathed Shaft from the ConveyorBelt into a Milled Shaft, which is then placed on the MobileRobot.

The Horizontal Milling Machine mills a Milled Shaft from the ConveyorBelt into a Finished Shaft for 79 minutes at a milling speed of 1000 rpm using a contour tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.4, then places the finished component on a MobileRobot.
